findings.text: The fragment cites station-tests.log as 'the failing arm at bae7b6ab8d', but that log's own header reads '# revision: bae7b6ab8db87dd75a00744cd097b51d7885d04b (working tree carries the moved judgement)' — the hard case this review's predecessor turned on. The arm is therefore bae7b6ab8d with the launch-record rule already present in the working tree, not the pre-commit state the sentence reads as; taken literally the citation shows the batch failing with the rule in place, which is the opposite of the sentence's claim. The claim itself survives on the two clean arms (station-combo-head.log at a clean 6c83e9f27f tree, 60 passed EXIT=0; station-combo-answering-reverted.log with 480a03a25b's session_host.py and station_subscriber.py reverted, 1 failed, 59 passed EXIT=1), so the citation should be corrected to describe the working-tree state or dropped.

The manifest's outside_scope still says 'population_has_live_work in reckon/crew/station_subscriber.py ... so the exclusion is made in this node's own judgement rather than by changing the shared rule', and rubric.scope_discipline says 'five staged paths'. Both deny the change commit 480a03a25b actually makes: it moves the launch-record exclusion into station_subscriber.live_work_populations, and changed_paths on the same manifest now lists reckon/crew/station_subscriber.py. A reader comparing the record to the diff finds the manifest denying the change it carries. This is the same defect the previous review recorded at this line; the gained commit did not address it.
